categories.main_business_segments: Veeva Systems operates two primary business segments: Commercial Solutions and R&D Solutions. Commercial Solutions include Veeva Commercial Cloud and Veeva Claims, focusing on sales, marketing, and medical affairs for life sciences companies. R&D Solutions encompass Veeva Development Cloud, Veeva RegulatoryOne, and Veeva QualityOne, supporting clinical, regulatory, quality, and safety functions in product development. The company also offers business consulting and professional services, and has a growing presence in the consumer products and chemical industries.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Veeva's core technologies are built on proprietary cloud platforms, primarily Veeva Vault, which enables content and data-centric applications for unified business processes. Some applications, such as Veeva CRM, have historically run on the Salesforce platform, but the company is migrating these to Veeva Vault. The company leverages multitenant cloud architecture, advanced data management, and integrates with third-party infrastructure providers like Amazon Web Services. Veeva emphasizes regulatory compliance, security (ISO 27001), and privacy (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA) in its software development and operations.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Veeva primarily serves the global life sciences industry, including pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and medical device companies, as well as contract research and contract sales organizations. Its customer base ranges from the largest multinational pharma companies (e.g., Bayer, Eli Lilly, Merck, Novartis) to emerging biotech firms. The company also addresses the consumer products and chemical industries with select applications for quality and regulatory management.
categories.geographic_coverage: Veeva operates globally, with significant revenues from North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, and additional presence in the Middle East, Africa, and Latin America. In fiscal 2023, 58% of revenues came from North America, 28% from Europe, and 14% from other regions. The company maintains data centers in the US, UK, EU, Japan, South Korea, and China, and serves customers in over 100 countries.
categories.supply_chain_position: Veeva operates as a downstream technology and service provider, delivering cloud-based software, data, and consulting solutions directly to end customers in the life sciences and related industries. It does not manufacture physical goods or operate in the physical supply chain, but rather enables digital transformation and compliance across R&D and commercial functions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Veeva's strategic focus is on deepening its role as the most strategic technology partner to the life sciences industry, with an emphasis on innovation in cloud-based solutions for R&D and commercial operations. The company invests heavily in R&D to expand functionality, usability, and regulatory compliance of its platforms, and is migrating key applications from Salesforce to its own Veeva Vault platform. Veeva also pursues growth in adjacent industries and continuous enhancement of data and analytics offerings.
categories.revenue_model: Veeva generates revenue primarily through subscription fees for its cloud-based software and data solutions, which are typically sold on a one-year or multi-year contract basis. Professional services (implementation, consulting, training) and business consulting provide additional revenue streams, generally billed on a time-and-materials or fixed-fee basis. In fiscal 2023, 80% of revenue came from subscriptions and 20% from services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Veeva is a market leader in industry cloud solutions for life sciences, with principal competitors including IQVIA (notably in CRM and data), Oracle, Dassault Systèmes, OpenText, Honeywell, and Microsoft. In data and analytics, it also competes with Ipsos and Definitive Health. Veeva differentiates itself through deep industry focus, regulatory expertise, and integrated cloud platforms, but faces competition from both specialized and general-purpose cloud providers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended January 31, 2023, Veeva reported $2.16 billion in total revenue, representing 16% year-over-year growth. Subscription services revenue was $1.73 billion (17% growth), and net income was $488 million. The company serves 1,388 customers and employs 6,744 people globally. While Veeva has demonstrated strong historical growth, it expects growth rates to moderate in future periods.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Veeva's value proposition centers on delivering industry-specific, cloud-based solutions that enable life sciences companies to accelerate product development, improve commercial effectiveness, and maintain regulatory compliance. Its deep domain expertise, rapid innovation, integrated data and content management, and commitment to customer success set it apart from generic cloud providers. Veeva emphasizes speed, reliability, and regulatory alignment as key differentiators.
